newsitem.title: USA: Orange County shifts more funds to annul bonds.
newsitem.headline: Orange County shifts more funds to annul bonds.

text.p: Orange County, Calif., supervisors on Thursday shifted $12 million more into a special account that could be used to defease county bankruptcy recovery bonds, a county spokeswoman said.
On Wednesday, the supervisors agreed to move $14.8 million into the special account.
With Thursday's funds, the account's balance comes to $26.8 million, county spokeswoman Diane Thomas said.
In June, the county Board of Supervisors authorized the chief executive officer to create the debt repayment account.
Orange County emerged from 18 months of bankruptcy in June following the successful sale of about $880 million of certificates of participation and bonds.
The county Board of Supervisors was expected to vote on the county budget for fiscal year 1996-1997 on September 24.
